thread:
alex: Pushing Day 0 of the slen-autotune canary. Goal: let the runtime pick arch-aware kernels based on seqlen distributions. Rolling to 10% on ampere clusters.

deploy-bot: Canary deployed: redwood-runtime/slen-autotune v3 -> 10% (canary@ampere). Logs streaming to /canary/2958765432

jordan: Quick heads-up: baseline throughput on shortctx (<=64) dropped ~8% vs control within first 5m. Scheduler CPU spiked. :eyes:

maya: Saw a lot of KV cache evictions in the canary traces. Prefill path is warming different keys than decode, causing cache churn when autotuner flips paths mid-request.

alex: Interesting — autotuner is switching to long-path kernels around seqlen ~80 due to a histogram shift. We probably don't want mid-request handoffs. Can we gate switching until KV warmup completes or until request boundary?

nick: From the flamegraphs, the extra cost is in `kv_lookup` + memcpy during handoff. If we delay path swap until the next request boundary that should avoid thrash. Also consider async prefetch of KV for predicted handoffs.

sam: Also noticed batching heuristics: dynamic batching is shrinking batch sizes for mixed-seqlen workloads, increasing per-token overhead. Quick trace command I used: `rbctl trace --canary --span=60 --filter=seqlen<128`

maya: Telemetry summary: percent of requests that experienced a path flip mid-stream = 3.4% (mostly between seqlen 60-96). Those have 1.5x p95 latency and 2x KV eviction rate compared to no-flip requests.

alex: Proposal: add hysteresis to the seqlen decision (require sustained median seqlen > threshold for N requests), and forbid mid-request kernel handoff. Expose config: `autotune.slen_hysteresis.window` and `autotune.prevent_mid_request_handoff` (default true).

jordan: +1. Also add metric `runtime.autotune.handoff.blocked` and a debug tag `autotune_reason=kv_warmup` so we can correlate with eviction spikes and batch size shifts.

deploy-bot: New canary patch queued: `slen-hysteresis-v1` -> will roll to 10% canary in 2m.

maya: After the patch, shortctx throughput returned to baseline within the first 30m and KV eviction spikes are down in the canary cohort. Continuing canary for 3 more hours and running a telemetry sweep across regions.

alex: Nice. Action items: 1) add unit/integration test that simulates mixed seqlen and asserts no mid-request kernel swap; 2) update runtime docs with autotune knobs; 3) instrument an A/B dashboard for `kv_eviction_rate` vs `handoff.blocked`. If anything else pops up we'll run a postmortem. Thanks all :thumbsup:
